overview: This is Polzeath’s main beach (Ordnance Survey and OpenStreetMap call the bay Hayle Bay). It’s a wide, flat stretch of sand right in front of the village, roughly 460 metres across, that runs a long way out at low tide, though most of it is covered at high water.

Polzeath is a lively little surfing village about ten kilometres north-west of Wadebridge, with shops, cafés and pubs along the seafront, and the beach is one of the busiest on this stretch of coast in summer.

expect.title: Surf
expect.text: The RNLI describes the surf here as good quality, and with some shelter from the wind the bay is busy with surfers of all kinds in summer.

expect.title: Wildlife
expect.text: Dolphins are sometimes seen in the bay, and the cliffs to the north are good for birdwatching, with puffins occasionally nesting on the offshore islands.

expect.title: Pentireglaze
expect.text: At the northern end, a smaller beach known locally as Baby Bay is cut off from the main beach by a rocky point at high tide.

goodToKnow.label: Tides
goodToKnow.text: The beach shrinks a lot at high tide, and on the biggest spring tides the sea can even flood the seafront car park.

goodToKnow.label: Coast path
goodToKnow.text: The South West Coast Path runs through the village, south to Daymer Bay and north out to Pentire Head.
